title: Diffusing to Coordinate: Efficient Online Multi-Agent Diffusion Policies
claim: A two-stage system decentralizes sampling through per-agent generative policies, then trains them jointly with a shared centralized critic.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, color-coded arrows showing data flow and gradients
description: Two large rounded panels. The left, light blue panel is titled 'Decentralized Execution & Data Collection'. It shows an Environment box, a Replay Buffer cylinder, and a stacked 'Agent i: Diffusion Policy' block. Inside the policy block, noise passes through denoise steps to an action. Thick blue arrows carry joint state, joint action and transition tuples around the loop. A large orange arrow leads from the buffer to the right panel, which is peach and titled 'Centralized Training'. That panel contains a Target Distributional Critic, a Centralized Distributional Critic with small distribution icons, a KL Loss box, a Policy Loss box, and another stacked diffusion-policy block. Orange arrows carry data (s, a, r, s'). A blue arrow carries the joint policy gradient. Green arrows lead to a summation box with an 'Auto Tuning' loop. A 'Stop Gradient' mark sits on the target critic's path. The eye goes first to the bold panel titles and the thick blue loop.
caption: The CTDE framework of OMAD. The left panel illustrates Decentralized Execution, where agents independently sample actions via a denoising diffusion process. The right panel depicts Centralized Training, where a shared Distributional Critic provides unified Value Guidance to jointly optimize policies, stabilized by adaptive regularization for the entropy evidence lower bound.
abstract: Online Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) is a prominent framework for efficient agent coordination. Crucially, enhancing policy expressiveness is pivotal for achieving superior performance. Diffusion-based generative models are well-positioned to meet this demand, having demonstrated remarkable expressiveness and multimodal representation in image generation and offline settings. Yet, their potential in online MARL remains largely under-explored. A major obstacle is that the intractable likelihoods of diffusion models impede entropy-based exploration and coordination. To tackle this challenge, we propose among the first \underline{O}nline off-policy \underline{MA}RL framework using \underline{D}iffusion policies (\textbf{OMAD}) to orchestrate coordination. Our key innovation is a relaxed policy objective that maximizes scaled joint entropy, facilitating effective exploration without relying on tractable likelihood. Complementing this, within the centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigm, we employ a joint distributional value function to optimize decentralized diffusion policies. It leverages tractable entropy-augmented targets to guide the simultaneous updates of diffusion policies, thereby ensuring stable coordination. Extensive evaluations on MPE and MAMuJoCo establish our method as the new state-of-the-art across $10$ diverse tasks, demonstrating a remarkable $2.5\times$ to $5\times$ improvement in sample efficiency.
